company.name: The New York Times
company.shortDescription: News from The New York Times, plus its puzzles, recipes, sports, and product reviews.
company.planHelp: Sign in at nytimes.com, click your initials or photo at the top right, then Account, then Subscription overview. That page names your plan, the price and the next billing date. If you subscribed through Apple or Google, you must cancel in that app store instead.

features.label: The news itself
features.question: Do you want to read New York Times news articles?
features.help: This is the main newspaper – news, opinion, and features. Every paid plan includes it.

features.label: Puzzles and games
features.question: Do you play the crossword, Wordle, Spelling Bee or the other puzzles?
features.help: The Times sells its puzzles on their own as well as inside the bigger subscription. If puzzles are the only thing you want, the separate Games subscription is much cheaper.

features.label: Recipes
features.question: Would you use the recipe collection?
features.help: Thousands of recipes with step-by-step instructions, and a place to save your favorites.

features.label: Sports coverage (The Athletic)
features.question: Do you follow a sports team closely?
features.help: The Athletic is a separate sports publication the Times owns, with reporters covering individual teams.

features.label: Product reviews (Wirecutter)
features.question: Do you like to read reviews before buying appliances or gadgets?
features.help: Wirecutter tests everyday products – kettles, mattresses, printers – and names a best pick.

features.label: Articles read aloud and podcasts
features.question: Would you rather listen to articles than read them on a screen?
features.help: Articles can be played as audio, and there are subscriber-only podcasts. Helpful if reading on a screen is tiring.

faq.q: Why does my New York Times bill suddenly go up?
faq.a: The Times advertises a low introductory rate – often for the first year – and then charges its standard rate automatically. Diary the date the introductory period ends. If the new price is more than you want to pay, telephoning or using the online chat to cancel very often produces an offer to keep you at a lower rate.

faq.q: I only want the crossword. Do I need the full subscription?
faq.a: No. The Times sells its puzzles as a separate, much cheaper Games subscription, and sells recipes separately as a Cooking subscription. If puzzles or recipes are all you want, ask for those rather than the full package.

faq.q: Why is the price shown per week?
faq.a: The Times quotes many of its prices as an amount per week but takes the money every four weeks, so you are billed thirteen times a year rather than twelve. Multiply the weekly figure by 52 to see what a year really costs.

faq.q: Can I get it free through my library?
faq.a: Often, yes. Many American public libraries and universities give members free digital access to The New York Times. It is worth asking at your local library before paying.
